processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Melted in a vacuum induction furnace under argon atmosphere and cast into ingot.
Homogenization at 1200 °C for 2 h, performed before forging/hot rolling.
Cast ingot forged to thick slab.
Forged slab hot rolled (HR) to 6 mm thickness.
HR plates heated to 1050 °C, isothermally held for 0.5 h, then quenched in water.
Cold rolled (CR) to 3 mm thickness, producing the CR (cold rolled) specimen.

structures.overall_structure: Austenite (FCC) - ferrite (BCC) duplex microstructure in the cold-rolled specimen. XRD shows clear austenite (FCC) and ferrite (BCC) diffraction peaks. The austenite matrix is largely deformed (cold rolled; GROD of austenite mostly 2°–180°) with only 7.9% recrystallized. Ferrite occurs in two morphologies: granular α ferrite at triple points of austenite grain boundaries and band-like δ ferrite elongated along the RD.

defects.lattice_distortion: Largely deformed austenite: GROD map dominated by pink/red (GROD 2°–180°), i.e. highly strained/deformed

microstructure_list.region: triple points of austenite grain boundaries

phases_present.morphology: granular, located at triple points of austenite grain boundaries
band-like, elongated along the RD; traced to the preceding HR structure and still present after solution treatment

measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: Flat dog-bone-shaped tensile specimens with a gage length of 25 mm, length direction along the rolling direction (RD)
measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Tensile tests at strain rate 10^-3 s^-1 at room temperature; three measurements per heat treatment, average taken. No tensile data reported for the CR specimen (Table 1 shows '-').

characterization_methods.purpose: Phase constituent identification of the CR structure and annealed structures
characterization_methods.key_findings: Diffraction peaks of austenite (FCC) and ferrite (BCC) were clearly observed in the CR sample; the CR sample shows FCC (111) near 43°, (200) near 50°, (220) near 74° and BCC (110) near 44.5° with a weak BCC (200) near 65°.

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Phase (PH) mappings and grain-reference-orientation-deviation (GROD) mappings of austenite; GROD threshold < 2° used to define recrystallized fraction; dark lines are high-angle austenite grain boundaries > 15°
characterization_methods.purpose: Phase mapping and determination of recrystallized austenite fraction, austenite grain size, and α/δ ferrite fractions
characterization_methods.key_findings: CR phase map: light-blue FCC matrix with red BCC regions and shear bands (elongated red features); CR GROD map: dominated by pink/red (GROD 2°–180°) indicating largely deformed austenite. Measured CR values: Rex-γ fraction 7.9%, γ grain size 15.38 ± 16.47 µm, α fraction 5.7%, δ fraction 5.4%.

computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: Temperature range 550–1400 °C for the designed duplex steel
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Calculated ferrite fraction remains almost constant at about 33% between 991 °C and 1250 °C and increases to a maximum as temperature decreases from 991 °C to 854 °C; in contrast the largest ferrite fraction measured by XRD appears at 900 °C and decreases above 900 °C, suggesting ferrite-to-austenite transformation.

unmapped_findings: The CR (cold rolled) specimen is the 3 mm thick cold-rolled sheet obtained by hot rolling the ingot to 6 mm, solution treating at 1050 °C for 0.5 h and water quenching, then cold rolling to 3 mm; it is the precursor/parent state from which all annealed DP specimens (DP950-1, DP950-5, DP1000-1, DP1000-5, DP1000-5-TD, DP1050-1) were produced (b0012).
No tensile properties are reported for the CR specimen: Table 1 lists '-' for YS, UTS, TE, SYS and SUTS of CR (b0019).

At 600 °C (a typical κ-carbide ageing temperature) no κ-carbide was detected in the XRD due to its limited fraction; β-Mn phase was found at 700–900 °C; κ-carbides and Cr7C3 carbides appeared at 950–1000 °C and disappeared at 1050 °C; annealing at 900 °C for 5 min gave the strongest BCC peaks (b0015).
The measured ultralow density of the developed material is 6.36 g·cm^-3 (buoyancy balance, Archimedes Principle), close to the previous record of 6.34 g·cm^-3 (b0012).

The ductile-to-brittle behavior related to α/γ and δ/γ interfaces, crack nucleation/deflection and δ-ferrite band orientation (Figs. 3–4) is reported for the annealed specimens (DP1000-5, DP1000-5-TD), not specifically for the CR specimen (b0027).
